answer: Every ship that enters the dry dock is written in the gate book with its name, its master and the day the gates closed behind it. A nebula docking claimed as logged fails the book: the gates must have shut at the walnut of the entry, and a ship never docked bears no dock mark on her keel. Buying a false docking costs a forger 9,400 in bribes to the dockmaster and fees to the yard, and the inlet book is kept for ten years, so a ship whose docking was never entered is turned away at the gates.
